review_flags.note: UPSC key marks (a) PSRQ. The most natural order is P S Q R (insulin released before 'on the other hand glucagon'), which is not among the options. Kept official key as final; founder may wish to exclude this item from learner practice or keep as printed.
UPSC key marks (b) RSPQ. The most natural order is S P Q R (S 'in three ways' introduces P, Q, R), which is not among the options. Kept official key as final.
UPSC key marks (c) 'accepted' as the opposite of 'expunged'. DP blind answer was (b) 'part of' (retained/included). The official key is kept; low-confidence item.
UPSC key marks (d) QPRS. DP blind answer was (a) SRPQ. Both orders are defensible; official key kept.

passages.title: Questions 1–5
passages.body: Post colonial cultural analysis has been concerned with the elaboration of theoretical structures that contest the previous dominant western ways of seeing things. A simple analogy would be with feminism, which has involved a comparable kind of project: there was a time when any book you might read, any speech you might hear, any film that you saw, was always told from the point of view of male. The woman was there, but she was always an object, never a subject. From what you would read, or the films you would see, the woman was always the one who was looked at. She was never the observing eye. For centuries it was assumed that women were less intelligent than men and that they did not merit the same degree of education. They were not allowed a vote in the political system. By the same token, what kind of knowledge developed by women was regarded as non-serious, trivial, gossip or alternatively as knowledge that had been discredited by science, such as superstition or traditional practices of childbirth or healing. All these attitudes were part of a larger system in which women were dominated, exploited, and physically abused by men. Slowly, but increasingly, from the end of 18th century, feminists began to contest this situation. The more they contested it, the more it became increasingly obvious that these attitudes extended into the whole of the culture; social relations, politics, law, medicine, the arts, popular and academic knowledge.
passages.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

passages.title: Questions 6–10
passages.body:
How wonderful is the living world! The wide range of the living types is amazing. The extraordinary habitats in which we find living organisms, be it cold mountains, deciduous forests, oceans, fresh water lakes, deserts or hot springs, leave us speechless. The beauty of a galloping horse, or a migrating bird, the valley of flowers or the attacking shark evokes awe and a deep sense of wonder. The ecological conflict and cooperation among members of a population and among populations of a community or even a molecular traffic inside a cell make us deeply reflect on – what indeed is life? This question has two implicit questions within it. The first is a technical one and seeks answer to what living is as opposed to the non-living, and the second is the philosophical one, and seeks answer to what the purpose of life is.

What is living? When we try to define 'living', we conventionally look for distinctive characteristics exhibited by living organisms. Growth, reproduction, ability to sense environment and mount a suitable response come to our mind immediately as unique features of living organisms. One can add a few more features like metabolism, ability to self-replicate, self-organize, interact and emergence to this list.
passages.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

passages.title: Questions 91–110
passages.body: The difficult thing about (91) _____ the science of habits is that most people, when they hear about this field of research, (92) _____ to know the secret formula for quickly changing any habit. If scientists have discovered how (93) _____ patterns work, then it stands to reason that they (94) _____ have also found a recipe for rapid change, right? If only it (95) _____ that easy. It's not (96) _____ these formulas don't exist. The problem is that there isn't one formula for (97) _____ habits. There are thousands. Individuals and habits are (98) _____ different, and so the specifics of diagnosing and changing the patterns in our lives differ from person to (99) _____ and behaviour to behaviour. Giving up cigarettes is different (100) _____ curbing overeating, which is different from changing how you communicate with your spouse, (101) _____ is different from how you prioritize tasks at work. What's more, each person's habits are (102) _____ by different cravings. As a result, this book does not (103) _____ one prescription. Rather, I hoped to deliver something else: a framework for understanding (104) _____ habits work and a guide to experimenting with how they (105) _____ change. Some habits yield easily to analysis and influence. Others are (106) _____ complex and obstinate, and require prolonged study. And for others, change is a (107) _____ that never fully concludes. But that does not (108) _____ it can't occur. Each chapter in this book explains a different aspect of why habits exist and how they function. The framework (109) _____ in this section is an attempt to distil, in (110) _____ very basic way, the tactics that researchers have found for diagnosing and shaping habits within our own lives.
passages.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Post colonialism is
questions.opt_a: a contestation of the then existing dominant western practices
questions.opt_b: a contestation of western practices in colonial states
questions.opt_c: a contestation of the superstitious practices
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The first sentence says post colonial analysis builds structures 'that contest the previous dominant western ways of seeing things'.
Step 2: (b), (c) and (d) add ideas the passage does not state.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What does '... she was always an object, never a subject' mean?
questions.opt_a: Women were given respect and worshipped
questions.opt_b: Women were not given any right equal to men
questions.opt_c: Women were treated at par with men
questions.opt_d: Women liked to be treated inferior to men
questions.explanation:
Concept: Interpreting a phrase in context.
Step 1: The passage says women were only looked at, never the 'observing eye', and were denied education and the vote.
Step 2: So being an object meant women were denied rights equal to men.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Why was 'she never the observing eye'?
questions.opt_a: She was beautiful, so she was observed by men
questions.opt_b: She liked to be observed by men
questions.opt_c: Women were assumed to be less intelligent than men
questions.opt_d: Women were assumed to be more intelligent than men
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the reason in the passage.
Step 1: 'For centuries it was assumed that women were less intelligent than men and that they did not merit the same degree of education.'
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The contestation to dominance of the male resulted in
questions.opt_a: participation of women in social relations, politics, law, medicine, the arts, popular and academic knowledge
questions.opt_b: participation of men in social relations, politics, law, medicine, the arts, popular and academic knowledge
questions.opt_c: participation of women in social movements
questions.opt_d: contestations with males in life leading to divorce
questions.explanation:
Concept: Cause and result.
Step 1: The more feminists contested male dominance, the more it became clear the attitudes extended into the whole culture. The result is women's participation in these fields.
Step 2: (b) wrongly says 'men'; (c) and (d) are not in the passage.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which word in the passage is opposite of 'contrast'?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym from the passage.
Step 1: To contrast is to show differences. An analogy shows similarity.
Step 2: The passage uses 'analogy' in 'A simple analogy would be with feminism'.
Answer: (d).

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Why are the living types amazing?

questions.opt_b: The living organisms are acting as per their interests
questions.opt_c: The human thinking makes the living types amazing
questions.opt_d: The evolution of life makes it amazing
questions.explanation:

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Why does the author say, 'ecological conflict and cooperation'?
questions.opt_a: Because living organisms are structured this way
questions.opt_b: Because ecological mechanism works with conflict and cooperation
questions.opt_c: Because humans want to fight and live together
questions.opt_d: Because living organisms sometimes fight and sometimes live together
questions.explanation:
Concept: Inference from a phrase.
Step 1: The phrase refers to 'conflict and cooperation among members of a population and among populations of a community'.
Step 2: That means organisms sometimes compete and sometimes live together. (b) is tempting but speaks of an 'ecological mechanism', which the passage does not say.
Step 3: UPSC's official key marks (d).
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true of the passage?
questions.opt_a: Meaning of life could be reflected as to what living is as opposed to the non-living and what the purpose of life is
questions.opt_b: Meaning of life could be reflected as to how living and non-living organisms exist
questions.opt_c: Meaning of life could be reflected as to where the life begins and where it ends
questions.opt_d: Meaning of life could be reflected on how various living organisms differ
questions.explanation:
Concept: Match with the author's statement.
Step 1: The question 'what indeed is life?' has a technical part (what living is as opposed to non-living) and a philosophical part (the purpose of life).
Answer: (a).

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Distinctive characteristics exhibited by organisms indicate that
questions.opt_c: they can be either living organisms or non-living organisms
questions.opt_d: they know the purpose of life
questions.explanation:
Concept: Inference.
Step 1: 'we conventionally look for distinctive characteristics exhibited by living organisms'. These features mark organisms as living.
Answer: (a).

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which word in the passage means 'unique'?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Vocabulary in context.
Step 1: 'Distinctive' means special to one kind, so it is nearest to 'unique'.
Step 2: 'Common' and 'general' are opposite in sense.
Answer: (c).

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The country's economy is growing and would continue to grow at a rapid pace in the coming years.
S6: The market share of electrical vehicles increases with increasing availability of infrastructure.
P: It also provides us an opportunity to grow as manufacturer of electric vehicles.
Q: According to NITI Aayog (2019), if India reaches an electric vehicle sales penetration, emission and oil savings can be achieved.
R: Given the commitments that India has made on the climate front as a nation and on environmental aspects, it is likely that larger and larger share of automobile sector would be in the form of electric vehicles.
S: This presents a great opportunity for the automobile industry as the demand for automobiles would only increase.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: S1 says the economy grows, so S ('This presents a great opportunity ... demand ... would only increase') follows. R then says more of that demand will be electric, Q gives NITI Aayog's view of electric vehicle penetration, and P adds the manufacturing opportunity, leading to S6.
Answer: (a) SRQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Central government receipts can broadly be divided into non-debt and debt receipts.
S6: This is also evident from the composition of non-debt receipts.
P: Debt receipts mostly consist of market borrowing and other liabilities which the government is obliged to repay in the future.
Q: The non-debt receipts comprise of tax revenue, non-tax revenue, recovery of loans and disinvestment receipts.
R: The outcomes as reflected in the Provisional Actual figures is lower than the budget estimate owing to reduction in the net tax revenue.
S: The Budget 2018-19 targeted significantly high growth in non-debt receipts of the Central Government, which was driven by robust growth.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: S1 names the two kinds of receipts. Q explains non-debt receipts and P explains debt receipts. R and S then discuss outcomes for non-debt receipts, leading to S6. UPSC's official key marks (d) QPRS.
Answer: (d) QPRS.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Palaeontology is the study of the remains of dead organisms over enormous spans of time.
S6: Faunal analysis gives information about the animal people hunted and domesticated, the age of animal at death, and the diseases that afflicted them.
P: Bones provide a great information.
Q: The distribution of faunal remains (animal bones) at a site can indicate which areas were used for butchering, cooking, eating, bone tool making and refuse dumping.
R: Within this discipline, molecular biology and DNA studies have been used to understand hominid evolution.
S: Hominid evolution answers the questions about what ancient people looked like, and to plot patterns of migration.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: 'Within this discipline' (R) refers to palaeontology in S1. S explains hominid evolution. P then moves to bones, Q gives bone distribution, and S6 on faunal analysis closes.
Answer: (c) RSPQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Hormones have several functions in the body.
S6: The two hormones together regulate the glucose level in the blood.
P: They help to maintain the balance of biological activities in the body.
Q: Insulin is released in response to the rapid rise in blood glucose level.
R: On the other hand hormone glucagon tends to increase the glucose level in the blood.
S: The role of insulin in keeping the blood glucose level within the narrow limit is an example of this function.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: P states the general function, and S gives insulin as an example. UPSC's official key marks (a) PSRQ, the only option that begins P, S. Note that Q (insulin released) reads more naturally before R (glucagon, 'on the other hand'), but no option offers P S Q R.
Answer: (a) PSRQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: All living things affect the living and non-living things around them.
S6: This interdependability needs to be understood when we, humans consume much more than required and abuse nature.
P: This can also affect the population of fox, if foxes depend on rabbits for food.
Q: For example, earthworms make burrows and worm casts.
R: This act of earthworms affects the soil, and therefore the plants growing in it.
S: Rabbit's fleas carry the virus which causes myxomatosis, so they can affect the size of the rabbit population.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: Q gives the earthworm example and R its effect on soil and plants. S gives a second example (rabbit's fleas) and P ('This can also affect ... fox') follows it, then S6.
Answer: (c) QRSP.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: The ecosystem of water is complex and many environmental factors are intricately linked.
S6: The trees slowly transfer rainwater into the sub-soil and this is critical for sustaining water for months after the rains.
P: Thick forests make for excellent catchments.
Q: The problems we see are because we have undermined these links over decades.
R: First, rain and snowfall are the only sources of water – about 99%.
S: In the four months of monsoon, there are about 30-35 downpours and the challenge is to hold this water in systems that can last us over 365 days.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: Q picks up 'links' from S1. R and S describe the sources and the challenge of holding water. P (thick forests as catchments) leads into S6 (trees transfer rainwater).
Answer: (a) QRSP.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Politics is exciting because people disagree.
S6: It is not solitary people who make politics and a good society; it is the people together which make good politics and society.
P: For Aristotle politics is an attempt to create a good society because politics is, above all, a social activity.
Q: They also disagree about how such matters should be resolved, how collective decision should be made and who should have a say.
R: They disagree about how they should live.
S: Who should get what? How should power and other resource be distributed? Should society be based on cooperation or conflict? And so on.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: R states what people disagree about, S gives examples, Q adds 'also disagree about how such matters should be resolved', and P (Aristotle) leads to S6.
Answer: (a) RSQP.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Regular exercise makes many of the organ systems become more efficient.
S6: Different activities require different levels of fitness.
P: It can improve your strength; make your body more flexible and less likely to suffer from sprain.
Q: It can also improve your endurance.
R: It also uses up energy and helps to prevent large amounts of fat building up in the body.
S: Exercise can increase your fitness in three ways.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: The three ways are strength and flexibility (P), endurance (Q) and using up energy (R), introduced by S 'in three ways'. The logical order is S P Q R, but that is not offered; UPSC's official key marks (b) RSPQ.
Answer: (b) RSPQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: On increasing the temperature of solids, the kinetic energy of the particles increases.
S6: The temperature at which a solid melts to become a liquid at the atmospheric pressure is called its melting point.
P: A stage is reached when the solid melts and is converted to a liquid.
Q: Due to the increase in kinetic energy, the particles start vibrating with greater speed.
R: The particles leave their fixed positions and start moving more freely.
S: The energy supplied by heat overcomes the forces of attraction between the particles.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: Heat raises kinetic energy (S1), so particles vibrate faster (Q). Heat overcomes attraction (S), particles move freely (R), and the solid melts (P), leading to the definition of melting point (S6).
Answer: (a) QSRP.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Things are often not what they seem.
S6: This happened without you even knowing. So imagine the changes that occur to this earth and humanity.
P: But you are really not, because the Milky Way galaxy, of which you are a part, is moving through space at 2.1 million kilometre an hour.
Q: So in roughly twenty second that it would have taken you to read this paragraph, you have already moved thousands of kilometre.
R: And that is without taking into account the effects of earth's rotation on its own axis, its orbiting around the sun and sun's journey around the Milky Way.
S: As you read this sentence, perhaps sitting in a comfortable chair in your study, you would probably consider yourself at rest.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, on the other hand).
Step 1: S sets up the belief of being at rest. P contradicts it (Milky Way speed), R adds more motions ('that is without taking into account'), and Q gives the distance moved, leading to S6.
Answer: (d) SPRQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

If I ______ a good match I would have got married.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Third conditional.
Step 1: The main clause 'would have got' is third conditional, so the if-clause takes the past perfect: 'had found'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The lady has been declared as one of the top ten ______ of the community.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Superlative with 'one of'.
Step 1: 'One of the top ten' needs a superlative and a plural noun: 'most powerful members'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

When I visited the villages nearby the city I ______ many water bodies intact.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Phrasal verb in the past.
Step 1: The visit is in the past, and 'came across' means found by chance.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He has lost all his investments and he is ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Word meaning.
Step 1: 'Broke' means having no money. 'Broken' describes a damaged object or a spirit.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He ______ whether he could get any certificate for the course.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Reported question.
Step 1: 'Whether' introduces an indirect question, so the verb is 'asked'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

I ______ farewell to all my course mates last year.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Past tense of 'bid'.
Step 1: The past tense of 'bid farewell' in this sense is 'bade'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Very few of the texts from very early Vedic period are ______ now.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Word meaning.
Step 1: 'Extant' means still existing.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

A speech is a ______ address, delivered to an audience that seeks to convince, persuade, inspire or inform.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Word meaning.
Step 1: A speech given to an audience to persuade or inform is a formal address.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

All that ______ is not gold.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Proverbs.
Step 1: The proverb is 'All that glitters is not gold'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Having been in politics for about 40 years, the party now treats him like ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Word meaning.
Step 1: A 'has-been' is a person whose best days are over.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

__Emboldened__ by its success, the leader now plans to go ahead with the plan and implementation.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Emboldened' means made bolder or more confident, so 'encouraged'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

It is encouraging to see India's __indigenous__ cinema is going places.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Indigenous' means native to a place, so 'home-grown'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The ability to imagine and conceive a common good is inconsistent with what is known as '__pleonexia__' is a major struggle for a good democracy to realize.
questions.opt_a: Greed to grab everything for oneself
questions.opt_b: Greed to accumulate more and more wealth
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Pleonexia' is an insatiable desire for more than one's share. UPSC's official key marks (a), 'greed to grab everything for oneself'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He tried to avoid saying something that would __implicate__ him further.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Implicate' means to show someone is involved in a wrong, so 'incriminate'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

The __statutory__ corporate tax which forms the major income of the government has not changed this year.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Statutory' means required or permitted by law, so 'legal'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

He has been part of the all __dissident__ activities.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: A dissident opposes official policy, so 'rebellious'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

__Advocacy__ is one major component of any new programme.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: Advocacy is public support or promotion of a cause.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

People avoided him for his __high mindedness__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'High-mindedness' means having strong moral principles.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

There is a __tendency__ to treat social changes as mere development in terms of accumulation of wealth.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: 'Tendency' means an inclination, so 'predisposition'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the underlined word.

During the ancient period poets were __patronized__ through various institutions.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Synonym.
Step 1: To patronize in this sense is to give financial or other support.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The __archaic__ thinking leads to unfounded beliefs.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Archaic' means very old-fashioned. Its opposite is 'modern'. The first three are synonyms.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Police had to resort to tear gas to __diffuse__ tension among the crowd.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Diffuse' means to spread out. Its opposite is 'concentrate'. 'Scatter', 'disperse' and 'strew' are synonyms.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

__Unrest__ in some pockets made the city dwellers confine themselves at home.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Unrest' is disturbance. Its opposite is 'calm'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

Peace and __tranquility__ are instruments which would boost the development of society.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Tranquility' is calmness. Its opposite is 'uproar'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

__Barring__ a decision of such disputes, other matters relating to the election of President or Vice-President may be regulated by law made by Parliament.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Barring' means excluding or except for. Its opposite is 'including'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

His speech was full of emotions and it was an __extempore__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Extempore' means spoken without preparation. Its opposite is 'prepared'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

The teacher asked her students to understand the __ensuing__ problems and address them suitably.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Ensuing' means following or coming after. 'Retrospective' looks back at what has gone before, so it is the opposite.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

All the allegations against the actor were __expunged__ by the committee of inquiry.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Expunged' means erased or removed. UPSC's official key marks (c) 'accepted' (the allegations were kept on record rather than removed). Note that (b) 'part of' can also be argued as an opposite.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

His relatives __dissuaded__ him from giving up the job.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: 'Dissuade' means to talk someone out of something. Its opposite is 'persuade'. The others are synonyms.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

He is one of the __confidants__ of the leader and can influence the decision of the government.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Antonym.
Step 1: A confidant is a trusted close friend. Its opposite is 'opponent'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

All the pilgrims rested for a while __under__ the banyan tree.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Under' comes before the noun phrase 'the banyan tree' and shows its position, so it is a preposition.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The wonderful __statue__ of the leader welcomes all people to city.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Statue' names a thing and is the subject of the sentence, so it is a noun.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

This is __his__ pen.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'His' comes before the noun 'pen' and tells whose it is, so it is a possessive adjective.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

When people found that the jewel was in records of Rahim, they gave __it__ to him.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'It' stands in place of 'the jewel', so it is a pronoun.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__It__ is eleven O'clock now and all of us should retire to bed.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'It' here refers to no particular person or thing; it is used for time, so it is an impersonal pronoun.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The flower is __very__ beautiful.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Very' modifies the adjective 'beautiful', so it is an adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__This__ boy is stronger than Ramesh.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'This' comes before the noun 'boy' and points to it, so it is a demonstrative adjective.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I hurt __myself__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Myself' refers back to the subject 'I', so it is a reflexive pronoun.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The ants __fought__ the wasps.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Fought' takes the object 'the wasps', so it is a transitive verb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

I can __hardly__ believe it.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Hardly' modifies the verb 'believe' and means 'almost not', so it is an adverb.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2020 English set A (set code DZOL-U-LKE – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Blank (91) of the passage
questions.explanation:
Concept: Cloze test (fit the blank to the sentence around it).
Step 1: 'The difficult thing about studying ...' needs the -ing form after the preposition 'about'.
Answer: (a).
